steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Sociology is the systematic study of society, social institutions, and social relationships. It investigates how society shapes human behaviour, attitudes and life chances. C. Wright Mills called this the 'sociological imagination' - seeing the link between personal troubles and public issues. | Key Fact: Sociology vs common sense: common sense is based on everyday assumptions; sociology uses systematic research methods and evidence. Example: common sense says crime is rising; official statistics show it has fallen since the 1990s. Sociology tests claims against evidence. | Key Fact: Social structures are the organised patterns of relationships and institutions that shape society: family, education, religion, economy, government.
